statements.verbatim_passage: Flame lengths >1.22 m are generally considered unsafe for crew to build hand lines; flame lengths >2.44 m are considered unsafe for engines or other ground-based equipment [41]. We classified POD boundaries with a 50% or more chance of having flame lengths >2.44 m as high-risk lines (HRLs) that might still be considered a PCL if the level of fire fighter risk is deemed acceptable, or that could be excluded from use when risk is deemed unacceptable.

statements.passage_as_proposed: We used the Fire Spread Probability (FSPro) model, which ingests topography, fuel data and daily fire weather forecasts during a fire event to stochastically simulate fire spread [31].
